beliefs: The box shifts each character forward by 8 codepoints, applied independently per character [E1, E2, E3, E6, E8]
The shift applies uniformly across ASCII, Latin-1, and multi-byte ranges including surrogates and near U+10FFFF [E6, E8]
In E4, the '~' (0x7E) that appears to map to '(' (0x28) is actually an artifact of the truncated/elided long-string display: the real output has 0x86 there, matching the uniform +8 rule [E9, E10]
E10's observed outputs match the uniform +8 rule exactly (the earlier E4 mismatch was a display/alignment artifact, not a real per-character rule) [E10]
notes: E10 shows the observed long-string outputs match plain +8 everywhere; the earlier E4 '~'->'(' discrepancy was an artifact of the truncated E4 display, not a real rule. So the model stays a uniform +8 shift, which already fits E1-E3 and E5-E10.
